title: Periodic ZnS/ZnSe Quarter-Wave Stack for MWIR Suppression with LWIR Pass
scientific_hypothesis: A 16-layer periodic stack of alternating ZnSe and ZnS, with optical thicknesses tuned to create a high-reflectance stopband centered near 4000 nm, will achieve transmittance above 80% in the 8000-11000 nm band while suppressing transmittance below 20% in the 3000-5000 nm band.
design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg reflectors produce maximum reflectance at the design wavelength where each layer has optical thickness λ/4. At wavelengths significantly longer than the design wavelength, the optical thickness becomes a smaller fraction of the wavelength, reducing the reflectance and allowing transmission. By centering the stopband at 4000 nm (middle of MWIR suppression band), the LWIR band (8000-11000 nm) falls in the transmission region beyond the stopband.
proposed_topology: Air | ZnSe(1) | ZnS(2) | ZnSe(3) | ZnS(4) | ZnSe(5) | ZnS(6) | ZnSe(7) | ZnS(8) | ZnSe(9) | ZnS(10) | ZnSe(11) | ZnS(12) | ZnSe(13) | ZnS(14) | ZnSe(15) | ZnS(16) | Ge substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 16 layers (t1 through t16 in nm)
Thickness ratio between ZnSe and ZnS layers within each pair
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band
Maintain smooth transmittance transition between bands to avoid sharp resonances
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 16 to meet the stated constraint
Layer thicknesses should remain above 200 nm for deposition uniformity
ZnSe and ZnS are both depositable by thermal evaporation or sputtering
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: ZnSe has higher refractive index than ZnS in the infrared region, providing moderate index contrast for Bragg reflection
Recalled knowledge: Germanium substrate has very high refractive index (~4.0 in IR), requiring anti-reflection consideration at the substrate interface
Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stack reflectance bandwidth scales with index contrast ratio; moderate contrast materials require more layers for deep suppression
Recalled knowledge: Absorption in ZnS and ZnSe is low in 3000-11000 nm range but increases toward longer wavelengths
Recalled design practice: Starting with high-index material at air interface improves match for high-reflector stacks
expected_advantages: Periodic structure simplifies optimization to thickness scaling rather than sequence search
16 layers provides sufficient pairs (8) for meaningful MWIR suppression with moderate index contrast
Quarter-wave centering at 4000 nm naturally creates LWIR passband without additional complexity
known_risks: Uncertain exact refractive index values for ZnS and ZnSe at 3000-11000 nm; actual index contrast may differ from recalled ~2.4 vs ~2.2
Uncertain whether Ge is resolvable in the material registry; if not, route will be rejected for repair
Uncertain absorption coefficients in LWIR band; ZnSe may have higher absorption than recalled at 11000 nm
16 layers may be insufficient for deep MWIR suppression if index contrast is lower than expected
No angle specification in request; assumed normal incidence but actual detector may have field-of-view requirements
The quarter-wave approach may create secondary transmission lobes in MWIR that reduce suppression effectiveness
execution_request_english: Design a 16-layer planar multilayer dielectric film on Germanium substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence from air side: ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS (16 layers total, alternating starting with ZnSe (Querry)). Optimize individual layer thicknesses for all 16 layers to maximize transmittance in 8000-11000 nm wavelength band while minimizing transmittance in 3000-5000 nm wavelength band. Use normal incidence (0 degrees). Materials: ZnSe (Querry), zns, Ge (Icenogle). Total layer count is fixed at 16. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, run_status, and thicknesses_nm for each optimization round.
